(n, &p): p := the first tone parameter of CONTROLLER page 2 controller n's 3-byte record {switches, destination, depth}: 0x14 0x17 0x1A 0x1D 0x20 0x25 0x28 0x2B 0x2E for n = 1..9, each 3 lower on a drum kit ((0x27F5) != 0).
ScreenEnter_SoundEditControllerPage2 keeps p in ModelingPage_Fields[13] and reads back p+2 (DEPTH -> Fields[11]) and p (switches -> Fields[12]); its nine destination requests are exactly p(n)+1. Basis: caller + body + the page's request list.

header:
(block e, reply): unpacks one 18-byte read-back of CONTROLLER page 1 (e = 0: parameters 0x31.., sources 1-3; e = 1: 0x43.., sources 4-6; drum 0x2E / 0x40), 6 bytes per source = two {switches, destination, depth} records: for the sources picked by the lowest set bit of Fields[5] / Fields[6] it stores the destinations Fields[1..4],
and for the picked controller (SoundEditController_LoadField0(1), 1..4) DEPTH -> Fields[11], switches -> Fields[12], record parameter -> Fields[13]. ScreenEnter_SoundEditControllerPage1 calls it on replies 3 and 4. Basis: caller + body + display records.

header:
(&slot): the SOUND EDIT MEMORY WRITE destination. The first time in a SOUND EDIT session (Var27F6 = 0) a sound already in user memory proposes its own place -- from the part record at 0x76A2 / 0x76E2 / 0x7722 (UI_PartIndex 0/1/2): bank 8/9 -> program + 128 x (bank - 8), drum bank 0x28 -> program 0..3 -- kept in (0x27E9) with Var27F6 := 1; otherwise the kept (0x27E9) (drum kit: reset to 0 when > 3).
ScreenEnter_SoundEditMemoryWrite makes it Fields[0] = slot / 128 + 1 (bank 1/2) and Fields[1] = slot % 128 + 1 (drum kit: Fields[1] = slot + 1). Basis: caller + body.
